extracted.intended_audience: researchers and academics who act as peer reviewers for journals (potential and current reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers serving as peer reviewers of journal research manuscripts on how to produce helpful, constructive, and reproducible reviews. Covers evaluative criteria (soundness, transparency, methodology, significance) plus practical reviewer behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate every statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantiate every statement — about a methodology weakness or about the significance of a result, with detailed arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When noting methodological weaknesses or commenting on the importance of results, provide detailed reasoning and evidence rather than unsupported assertions; explain why something is problematic or why a claim is or isn't justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a constructive tone even when there is a lot to criticise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase criticisms to help authors improve the manuscript; avoid hostile, dismissive, or unprofessional language that doesn't contribute to revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify technical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify technical soundness — manuscript is technically sound and claims sufficiently supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check analyses, data interpretation, and whether conclusions follow from results; identify missing controls, statistical errors, or overinterpretation and request clarifications or additional work where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for transparency — enough detail that other groups have, in principle, enough information to repeat the experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure methods, protocols, and data availability are described with sufficient detail for reproducibility; flag missing methodological details, unavailable data, or unclear procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess methodology appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess methodology appropriateness — is the methodology appropriate for the question?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the experimental design, chosen methods, and statistical approaches are suitable to address the research question, and whether alternative methods might be more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent about expertise limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent about expertise limits — explicitly state the limits of your technical expertise in your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare areas outside your expertise so editors can weigh your comments appropriately; avoid making definitive judgments on aspects you are not qualified to assess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contextual significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contextual significance — give specific context on the significance of the results and interpretations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the findings fit into the broader literature, why they matter, and what the realistic impact is; avoid vague claims about importance without supporting rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know when to decline
rubrics_metrics.description: Know when to decline — acknowledge time / conflicts rather than accepting every request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you lack time, have a conflict of interest, or lack sufficient expertise, decline promptly so editors can find alternative reviewers; declining is preferable to providing a low-quality or rushed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggest alternatives — recommend a well-qualified colleague when declining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When declining, offer names and contact details of suitable alternative reviewers if possible to help editors identify replacements quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain visibility — keep a clear online record (homepage, Google Scholar, ORCID) so editors can find you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep professional profiles updated (ORCID, institutional page, Google Scholar) so editors can verify expertise and invite you appropriately.
